title: Annotatio III §.X (6) close: Natural humanity — corporal chewing of Christ’s flesh vs Lev. blood ban; stop before §.XI (7) Sense
pass_a_gloss: Then NATURAL and common HUMANITY also, by stating and commanding Christ’s human Flesh to be eaten with the corporal mouth and His human blood to be drawn and drunk with the corporal mouth — by this pact commanding Actions from which human Nature, not yet degenerated into the brute, spontaneously abhors; and that it might abhor the more certainly, once among the Jewish people it is read to have been expressly guarded by GOD’s precept that one must abstain from all blood of living things, Lev. 7:27 and ch. 17:14.
pass_b_english: It also butts natural common humanity: commanding Christ’s human flesh chewed and His blood drunk with the corporal mouth — acts unfallen human nature spontaneously abhors.
God once expressly barred the Jewish people from all animal blood (Lev. 7:27; 17:14) so that abhorrence would be the surer.
source_text: Dein HUMANITATEM QUOQUE NATURALEM Communemque, statuendo jubendoque Carnem Christi humanam, corporali ore manducandam & sanguinem ejus humanum, ore corporali hauriendum bibendumque, Actiones hoc pacto imperando, à quibus humana Natura, nondum in brutam degenerata, sponte suâ abhorret & ut abhorreret tantò certiùs, olim, in gente Judaica, ab omni animantium sanguine abstinendum esse, disertô à DEO præcepto cautum fuisse legitur, Lev. 7. vers. 27. & cap. 17. 14.

lemmas.gloss: from all blood of living things
